findings.title: Deduplicate the active run IDs before filtering executions
findings.summary: `TestExecution.objects.filter(run__in=active_run_ids)` is driven by a Python list of run IDs built from each stream’s active runs, so the same run IDs are re-fed to the next query without being deduplicated explicitly.

suggestion.rationale: If the run-ID list can contain duplicates, removing them before the filter keeps the same matching set while giving the ORM a smaller `IN (...)` list to process.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: The set of matching executions is unchanged because `run__in` depends on membership, not multiplicity. Row ordering is irrelevant to the aggregate, columns are unchanged, and NULL handling is unaffected because the same run IDs still participate. Duplicate handling is preserved at the query result level because the aggregate is over the same unique run set.
assumptions: `active_run_ids` may contain duplicates from earlier data gathering steps.
The aggregate does not depend on the multiplicity of IDs in the `IN` list.
suggestion.expectedImpact: A smaller `IN` list for the aggregate and less redundant matching work in the database parser/planner.

verified: Neither version orders its rows, so neither guarantees an order.
The filter expressions are textually unchanged.
equivalence.summary: Verified (django): every mechanically decidable property of the result is identical.

unmeasured: Whether this is actually faster. speeDB does not execute anything — it has no connection, no timings and no query plan.

findings.title: Prefer a single filter for matching cases
findings.summary: `pk__in` plus `case_status__is_confirmed=True` already returns the same rows as the current query, but the current shape forces the ORM to build the same predicate in two steps.

suggestion.rationale: This keeps the same predicate and ordering, but groups the filtering conditions in a way that is easier for the ORM to read and preserve as a single SQL WHERE clause.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: It returns the same rows because the same two conditions are applied. The selected columns, ordering, NULL handling, duplicates, and errors are unchanged because this is only a reordering of keyword arguments.
assumptions: MySQL is the intended dialect, as detected in the site metadata.
No downstream code depends on the textual form of the queryset object.
suggestion.expectedImpact: No row-shape change; the database still evaluates one filtered query and can use the same indexes available to the original predicate.
